facts.text: Kincheloe grew from a lumbering town and railroad hub in the late 19th century, with the township formally established in 1899.
The town sits on the former Kincheloe Air Force Base, a 7,265‑acre Strategic Air Command site that once covered 7,265 acres.
The base began as Kinross Auxiliary Airfield in 1941 to refuel Alaska‑bound aircraft, later expanding into a major Cold War installation.
The Oaks at Kincheloe golf course started as a nine‑hole course built by the base in 1951 and grew to 18 holes in 1987.
Environmental investigations continue at former base sites due to PFAS contamination in groundwater affecting local wells.
Kincheloe lies at the eastern end of Kinross Charter Township, just east of I‑75 and about 20 miles southwest of Sault Ste. Marie.
